name: smartflow-beta
responsibility: Package the complete WESEO SmartFlow workflow for WordPress/WST projects in one plugin: server-side WordPress and WST foundations, Section and CPT work, local frontend CSS/SCSS implementation, Playwright QA, and the documentation layer. Successor to the six legacy packages wordpress-server-ops, wst-builder, frontend-design-qa, and their -beta twins.
assumptions: The plugin is used in a Cursor workspace whose repository root is the wp-content level of a WESEO WordPress/WST project checkout; only the child theme subdirectory is deployed to the server.

Installing smartflow (or smartflow-beta) replaces all six legacy packages: wordpress-server-ops, wst-builder, frontend-design-qa, and their -beta twins. The plugin must not run next to any legacy package, and smartflow and smartflow-beta must never run together.

Project-specific CPT names, URL slugs, ACF keys, WPGB IDs, WordPress paths, URLs, credentials placeholders, and learned quirks live in the project-local PROJECT-CONTEXT.md and the project docs/ layer, never in reusable plugin content.

The agent never pushes unprompted: it commits and hands over to the user, who pushes to the remote (an explicit per-request user instruction in the current chat can allow a push on a non-protected branch); deployment reaches the server through the project deploy path and is verified over the project status bridge before QA continues.

rules.name: plugin-package-boundary
rules.description: Keep required SmartFlow workflows self-contained inside the plugin package and prevent development-only path dependencies.

rules.name: status-bridge
rules.description: Use the project status bridge (REST namespace wso/v1) for deploy verification, cache flush, permalink flush, and WP Grid Builder grid/card/facet read-write (wpgb/* routes since bridge 1.1.0; the single-item GET needs >= 1.1.1 on WPGB 2.x where the exporter class is gone: read-modify-write with re-read proof, create by cloning a GET never by invented columns, string reference ids (cards.default, grid_layout facets), css never decoded, name/slug uniqueness before create, card before grid, reindex after facet writes, cache flush after write passes), and enforce the mandatory bridge version comparison and deployed-commit check before every bridge use, with a bounded retry and abort budget. Opens with a plain-language definition of the bridge and names .wso-deployed-commit as the deploy-marker file (not a CSS class) wherever it appears. The WPGB write routes wrap undocumented WPGB internals and are the first suspect after a WPGB plugin update. Replaces the legacy wp-cli-cache flush path.

rules.name: webroot-safety
rules.description: Keep non-source artifacts out of the deployed child theme path: the wp-content-level repository root is never served, so only the deploy path needs webroot precautions. Shrunk from the legacy full-webroot rule to the deploy-path boundary.

rules.name: deploy-and-branches
rules.description: SmartFlow deploy flow and branch discipline: the agent never pushes unprompted and never commits on its own - every commit is prepared (files, summary, proposed message) and happens only after an explicit user confirmation, with scoped standing mandates only where a Skill explicitly asks for one; a push is allowed only on a non-protected branch after an explicit per-request user instruction in the current chat (never a standing mandate, never main/master/trunk), followed by the same bridge verification as after a user push; deploy-needing work is bundled into one pass with a hard stop after the confirmed commit; the deploy is verified over the status bridge before any served QA pass. main/master/trunk are write-protected (no commit, merge, or revert there, and push-forbidden even with explicit instruction), and the prohibitions propagate explicitly into every subagent worker prompt. Working Tree Discipline: the agent never discards, restores, stashes, or cleans uncommitted changes it did not make in this run - unexpected files are reported by path against a git status baseline, never staged or touched, and a discard needs an explicit file-naming user confirmation; runners revert only their own edits inside their write scope. Recognizes the legacy support state 'Working branch: master - user commits' (recorded by setup-ticket-ready): the agent prepares the commit and hands over, the colleague commits and pushes - never a per-ticket contradiction stop. Absorbs the protected-branches rule from the legacy skill zip.

rules.name: secrets
rules.description: Secret handling for SmartFlow repositories: the tracked repo-root .env pushed to the private remote is a deliberate accepted decision, and secrets enter commands exclusively through environment variables, never as literals in tracked files, chat, logs, or docs.

rules.name: acf-local-json
rules.description: Author all project-owned ACF field definitions as Local JSON files under acf-json/ in the child theme: admin stays editable, agents write JSON with a modified bump, a human confirms every structural change with a sync click. Binding operating rules (pull-before-deploy over read-only FTP - implemented by the pre-commit hook from setup-acf-local-json Step 8, JSON as the only agent write path, sync only after diff review), the modified rule (real current UTC epoch via python time.time(), never a computed or future value - a future modified makes the sync hint permanent), the clone-and-conditional-logic pattern (no conditional_logic on seamless clone fields; variant switches via a local tab field in exclusion form inside one group; clone source field keys never carry the source tab), the fixed German admin-sync hand-over text for colleagues (collective sync, then one unchanged save per group, Abbrechen on a second hint), the verification boundary 'implementation pass, backend check by colleague pending', plus the ACF 6 encode style as default (raw UTF-8, escaped slashes, LF plus trailing newline, one-pass serialization; a differing write format recorded in PROJECT-CONTEXT.md wins), the ACF Extended autosync opt-in (nested acfe.autosync default, legacy top-level acfe_autosync recognized, never guessed), the empirical per-installation write-format determination, a JSON conventions checklist, and the mandatory wso_ field-name prefix for CPT fields (wso_<resource>_<field>, for example wso_job_salary on a Job CPT). Structural ACF database writes stay forbidden entirely. Replaces the retired acf-php-field-groups rule and the PHP migration scaffold.

rules.name: file-edit-boundary
rules.description: Restrict edits in the wp-content-level repository to approved source paths: child theme incl. WST source and the ACF Local JSON definitions under acf-json/, docs layer, workspace config; WST plugin folder, third-party code, uploads, and direct server edits stay off-limits; functions.php is forbidden and theme-functions.php needs explicit confirmation.

rules.name: commit-trailer
rules.description: Apply the commit trailer `Made with: SmartFlow` to every SmartFlow-authored commit in the commit-and-hand-over flow.

rules.name: css-guideline
rules.description: CSS and SCSS conventions for WESEO frontend implementation: tokens, selectors, rem scaling, responsive strategy, and the two proof modes injection-proof and bridge-verified served check (deployed_commit match over the status bridge) replacing the legacy source-served verification.

rules.name: figma-to-code
rules.description: Rules for translating Figma designs into frontend code: grid translation, spacing, typography, image behavior, and Figma-comparison proof modes injection-proof and bridge-verified served check.

rules.name: wst-php-authoring-route
rules.description: Route child-theme PHP authoring through the WST workflows and the wst-shortcode-implementer subagent; template output composes existing WST shortcodes and follows verified precedent.

rules.name: frontend-section-qa-layout-preflight
rules.description: Layout preflight before the CSS pass: extract the Figma layout model (paradigm, sizes, gaps, min width, typography), run the container fit check, and fill the Playwright px measurement matrix before and after the injection proof.

rules.name: frontend-section-qa-tablet-band
rules.description: Require the full QA viewport ladder (desktop and mobile Figma anchors plus intermediate rungs) with deliberate 768-991px tablet-band styling before any final frontend Section or CPT QA pass; rung values reconciled with PROJECT-CONTEXT.md.

rules.name: playwright-browser-claim
rules.description: Playwright MCP browser availability for every browser use (single server included): namespace check via GetDynamicTools before the first browser call (absent namespace = server deregistered after an mcp.json change, manual restart under Settings > Tools & MCP, never treated as loading), the SingletonLock / 'Browser is already in use' diagnosis (read the PID, check for an orphaned Chromium, ask before ending a process, --isolated as the durable fix), transient Cursor tool errors ('Timeout waiting for bubble creation' / 'Failed to find tool call context' shown as User rejected MCP) retried twice before reporting, no silent substitute browser (cursor-ide-browser never sets a pass), and the Node 18.17 floor - plus the claim/release protocol over .cursor/pw-locks/ for workspaces running parallel Playwright MCP servers, so concurrent agents never share or steal a browser.

rules.name: runner-gate
rules.description: Always-on hard gate for the four runner-backed Skills: wst-section-workflow and wst-new-post-type execute only inside the wst-shortcode-implementer, frontend-section-qa and cpt-frontend-qa only inside the cpt-visual-implementer; the main chat prepares the record, spawns exactly one runner per Section or surface with a self-contained prompt, and runs deploy pass and commit gate. Hard stop before the first CSS/WST/ACF write or Playwright call when the current agent is not the runner; the non-reasons list (loaded Skill text, material already in context, 'nur Styling', prior main-chat work, 'one leaf is enough'); the re-route check after a context break with the current file state as runner input; and the prompt split for mixed requests. agent-routing stays the detail source.

rules.name: wordpress-brand-tokens
rules.description: Enforce project brand-token usage instead of hardcoded brand colors in theme CSS and WST templates, with centralized per-brand palettes keyed to the company-taxonomy body class.

rules.name: wordpress-taxonomies
rules.description: Author WordPress taxonomies the WESEO way: English wso_tax_ machine names, German labels allowed, CPT UI managed registration prepared for the user, code only for what CPT UI cannot do, permalink flush through the status bridge.

rules.name: wst-conditional-nesting
rules.description: WST conditional shortcodes must never nest the same tag name directly; use the named-level chain and prefer wst_include for shared partials to avoid silent pairing failures.

rules.name: wordpress-content-editing
rules.description: Safely edit WordPress page, post, and options content over REST when the project uses ACF Flexible Content: read first, preserve the full array, change only requested fields, normalize types, UTF-8 JSON, no structural ACF or template writes.

rules.name: agent-routing
rules.description: Route SmartFlow WST/CPT package work, Jira batch ticket work, grid-cards write routing, and generic worker orchestration to the six bundled subagents: the package definitions (CPT package, package run, package manifest; package orchestration is not a separate mode — every routing statement applies on every start), delegation table with write scopes, recommended-model routing with dynamic pinning at spawn (agent files ship model: inherit, so spawns never fail on a missing model; available recommended slugs are passed at spawn, deviations reported in one sentence, never silently substituted), the deliberately-not-routed scope (now including smartflow-feedback and sync-project-brief as interactive main-chat Skills; the preview harness returns from runners as OPEN DECISION: preview-offer or preview-fixtures, and no orchestrator prompt may forbid touching an active harness unless declined), the runner as the standard execution vehicle for the four runner-backed Skills even on direct starts with the explicit non-reasons for skipping it (mirrored by the always-on runner-gate Rule) plus the analyst spawn conditions of the two discovery agents, orchestrator/handoff practices adapted from rekursiv (self-contained prompts carrying the Working Tree Discipline, context-full continuation via STATUS handoff, stall stop, integration check of git status against the run baseline - unexplained changes reported, never discarded), and the shared fixed return contract.

rules.name: confluence-source
rules.description: Confluence as the leading project source: the PL Umsetzung page is anchored once in PROJECT-CONTEXT.md (page ID, URL, mirror timestamp), read at exactly three points (setup-local-project mirrors, the four work-package Skills re-read fresh at run start, runners stay offline with the distilled extract in their prompt), extraction instead of template enforcement (optional text status markers and Fuer-Cursor block recognized, decision chains resolved to the newest statement), controlled refresh only through sync-project-brief, and secrets never mirrored - placeholder plus pointer instead.

rules.name: feedback-capture
rules.description: Always-on trigger moments for the proactive feedback offer: when a run step demonstrably deviated from a bundled Skill's or Rule's promise (wrong classification, missed hard stop, manual user correction, wrong bundled reference), the agent offers exactly one sentence at the hand-over point and runs smartflow-feedback on yes. Hard annoyance guards: only real detected deviations, one sentence, never blocking, never mid-run, once per deviation, never auto-report.

rules.name: jira-comment-signature
rules.source: Confluence Verbesserungsideen: SmartFlow feedback hub, page 1982857256
rules.description: End every automatically created Jira comment (solution comments, transition/occurrence notes, worklog comments over jira_add_comment and jira_edit_comment) with its own last line '– erstellt mit SmartFlow'; never appended twice, and not applied to Confluence comments, which keep their own intake format.

skills.name: install-status-bridge
skills.description: Install or update the versioned SmartFlow status bridge in the child theme's js-snippets.php from the bundled PHP template (wso/v1/status with bridge_version, deployed_commit, ACF field groups, WPGB grids, and cache state, plus cache flush, permalink flush, and since bridge 1.1.0 the WPGB read/write routes wpgb/<type> list, read, create, and update plus wpgb/reindex, all behind manage_options; bridge 1.1.1 adds the WPGB 2.x fallback for the single-item GET via Database::query_row because WPGB 2.x removed the exporter class): a plain-German explanation of what the bridge is for the user before the first install step (what it does, that it is deployed like any theme file, that .wso-deployed-commit is a marker file and not a CSS class), managed-block install, deployed-commit file contract, commit-and-hand-over stop, and post-deploy verification over wso/v1/status. The normal update path (marker version comparison, block replacement) rolls new bridge versions out to existing projects without extra steps.

skills.name: setup-local-project
skills.description: Guided German wizard for the complete first setup of a local SmartFlow workspace: clone the wp-content-level repository, name the folder exactly after the server hostname (DevTools Local Overrides), fill the tracked .env with the application password, run the REST test, verify Atlassian MCP with the community mcp-atlassian preflight (community mcp-atlassian server version 0.22.0 or newer as team standard - the version floor is a security requirement, local stdio only, token in the env block never in args; a working legacy Rovo server stays a functioning read variant), anchor the project's Confluence page and mirror its extract into PROJECT-CONTEXT.md per the confluence-source Rule (no page is a valid state), find and follow the current Confluence weseo-git-installer guide via search, create the read-only FTP user with .ftpaccess (verified read-works/write-denied), install the status bridge, expose post types, taxonomies, ACF field groups, and ACF options pages over REST (bundled wso/v1/options endpoints and the full connection test, absorbed from the legacy setup-wordpress-cursor skill), configure Playwright MCP (isolated in-memory browser profile via --isolated, Node 18.17 floor as a blocker, and the rule that every mcp.json change ends with a manual server restart under Settings > Tools & MCP plus a namespace re-check - also stated for the Atlassian and Figma steps), verify Figma MCP, record the current Motherboard hostname from the Erstinstallation Confluence page as Cloned from (clone model: every project starts as a Motherboard clone; do not ask the user for a master-install name) and write the css_setup pending marker pointing at the project-css-setup pass shortly before the first Section, fill PROJECT-CONTEXT.md with deploy branch and bridge version, and close with the two setup gates in this order: the ACF Local JSON workflow first (Step 14, routed to setup-acf-local-json, gate acf_local_json — skipped only by explicit user decision, never silently; hand-over with the fixed admin-sync text from the acf-local-json Rule), then the docs layer (Step 15, first auto-docs run, gate docs_layer, with the fallback 'done (field-groups pending: rerun auto-docs after acf_local_json)' when the ACF gate is still open), because auto-docs documents field groups from acf-json/. Successor to the legacy Remote-SSH setup-orientation. For pure support work the bundled setup-ticket-ready lite track is enough; this wizard resumes a lite-prepared project at its pending: Voll-Setup markers.

skills.name: setup-ticket-ready
skills.source: Confluence Skill-Einreichungen: [Skill] setup-ticket-ready, page 1971191811 (grill-me decision log, Fandler WP-42325)
skills.description: Bring a project to a ticket-ready state in minutes as the lite setup track of setup-local-project: only the six mandatory gates without which no support ticket works (repo clone with hostname folder, .env plus REST test with manage_options, minimal PROJECT-CONTEXT.md with URLs, theme path, deploy path, Jira key, and working branch, working-branch resolution including the recognized legacy state 'Working branch: master - user commits', Atlassian MCP with Jira as the blocking surface, Playwright MCP with the same --isolated template and restart-and-verify rule as the full wizard). The repo-clone gate activates an existing .githooks/pre-commit ACF pull hook via core.hooksPath. On-first-need gates (status bridge, Figma MCP, Confluence anchor) are recorded as pending: on first need and set up the moment a ticket needs them; the consciously excluded full-setup gates (git-installer, read-only FTP, options REST, .wso-deployed-commit, css_setup marker, ACF Local JSON via setup-acf-local-json and after it the docs layer via auto-docs) stay pending: Voll-Setup so setup-local-project can resume there without a break. Resumable, same PROJECT-CONTEXT.md schema, runs standalone or as step 0 gate check of jira-ticket-workflow; deploy proof without a bridge runs over the marker-based served check.

skills.name: setup-acf-local-json
skills.description: One-time setup of the ACF Local JSON workflow in a SmartFlow project: bridge inventory (participants local false, plugin groups local php excluded), acf-json/ in the child theme without any code change plus the gitattributes eol=lf recommendation, seed split from a user-driven ACF admin export (ACF 6 encode style with raw UTF-8 and escaped slashes, one-pass serialization, no modified timestamps, keys reconciled), the ACF Extended autosync opt-in fix (nested acfe.autosync default, legacy top-level shape recognized) with a one-time collective sync, empirical determination of the canonical write format at the first admin save (filename, unicode escaping, autosync shape, newlines - recorded in PROJECT-CONTEXT.md), both-direction functional proofs, acceptance over an FTP hash comparison plus the bridge listing all participants as local json, and Step 8: the pull-before-deploy pre-commit hook (bundled asset pre-commit-acf-json-pull.sh, repo-level .githooks/ with core.hooksPath, FTP credentials from .env via netrc, per-key merge of server changes, modified guard, --dry-run and ACF_JSON_PULL_SKIP escape hatch; recorded as acf_json_pull_hook and ftp_acf_json_path in PROJECT-CONTEXT.md).

skills.name: migrate-ssh-to-local
skills.description: Self-contained one-time migration of an existing project from the legacy Remote-SSH plus WP Pusher model to the local SmartFlow model. Export stage in the SSH workspace: inventory, the ACF admin JSON export as the Local JSON seed source (nothing deleted, nothing converted), migration bundle outside the webroot. Import stage locally: setup-local-project foundation, theme and docs import with FTP diff, PROJECT-CONTEXT.md translation, WP Pusher teardown, git-installer build-up, ACF Local JSON setup via setup-acf-local-json, and bridge-verified acceptance with the project groups listed as local json.

skills.name: project-css-setup
skills.description: Reconcile a project's global theme CSS values with its Figma design in one resumable pass: four blocks in fixed order (content widths, fonts, colors/brand tokens, buttons and global spacing), each running extract from the design, compare with the theme, per-value confirmation, injection-proofed write, and viewport-ladder verification. Reads the css_setup marker in PROJECT-CONTEXT.md (master-values mode sets directly from the design; adapted mode shows the theme-vs-design diff and the user decides per value), builds an impact map before every change (docs-layer work records plus var() consumer search; the affected-Sections list is shown in the confirmation, becomes the post-change spot-check plan, and doc gaps are written back), derives values once at the 1920 design anchor and lets the fluid rem basis scale (bundled measurement reference with the 991-at-990 Playwright caveat, 375 as second anchor, targeted per-breakpoint overrides only where a rung visually fails), flips the marker to reconciled when at minimum the widths block is done, and ends in one bundled commit with hard stop. Runs in the main chat by design (interactive per-value confirmations, deliberately not routed).

skills.name: wst-section-workflow
skills.description: Single entry point for WST Flexible Content Section work in the local workspace: classification (new foundation, remodel, visual-only) from three neutral start questions with the same-purpose rule (an existing Section serving the same purpose is remodeled, never paralleled by a new slug) and a mandatory foundation-confirmation stop before the first tracked write, pattern discovery with the four-source proof per nesting context ('proven except runtime' named in the deploy hand-over), Section templates plus ACF Local JSON field groups (clone/tab pattern for variant switches, real UTC modified) and Flexible Content wiring as tracked source, an existing-Section remodel checklist, one bundled deploy pass with pull-before-deploy, commit-and-hand-over stop, bridge-verified served verification, and the human sync click for field-definition changes, the three-state preview-harness handling (missing = offer; active = mandatory per-Section fixtures block with exporter config, backend review stop, export, and preview URLs before frontend QA; declined = skip), and the Section work record in the project docs layer that routes to frontend-section-qa via the cpt-visual-implementer. At run start the anchored Confluence page is re-read fresh and only the Section-relevant extract lands in the work record (clean skip without anchor, per the confluence-source Rule). On every start — direct start included — the main chat orchestrates (classification, pattern-discovery decision, work record, hard stops) while the execution run of template and ACF JSON writes runs through the wst-shortcode-implementer runner per the agent-routing and runner-gate Rules; routine single-Section discovery deliberately stays in the main chat, with heavy Figma extraction delegated to the cpt-figma-analyst.

skills.name: wst-new-post-type
skills.description: Single entry point for WST Custom Post Type work in the local workspace: preflight as write gate, three delivery paths (tracked source for templates and ACF Local JSON field groups over the bundled deploy pass plus the human sync; CPT UI, taxonomy, WPGB, and Smart Template single-assignment apply-specs for the user; bridge flushes), remodel protections, and the CPT work record in the project docs layer that routes to cpt-frontend-qa. CPT detail pages render only through the Smart Template assignment (single partial plus the wst_include one-liner in the Smart Template's top-level code editor), never through the WordPress template hierarchy or theme-functions.php workarounds; single partials use typed ACF shortcodes because generic wst_acf resolves empty in the include context. For CPTs with detail pages the preflight asks the mandatory content-model question verbatim (typed-only | flexible-content-only | hybrid, never defaulted) with the analysts' evidence attached - the reference CPT's Flexible Content clone from the codebase analyst and the ordered detail-page walk with per-segment content-roles from the Figma analyst; hybrid adds the [TMPL] Flexible Inhalte clone (wso_<resource>_content, prefix_name 1) to the CPT group and renders the FC include as a sibling after the single partial's wrapper, and a typed-only remodel whose design shows page Sections is flagged with a hybrid proposal instead of hardcoded includes. At preflight start the anchored Confluence page is re-read fresh and only the CPT-relevant extract lands in the work-record draft (clean skip without anchor, per the confluence-source Rule). On every start — direct start included — the main chat orchestrates (classification, preflight, work record, hard stops) while the foundation execution run runs through the wst-shortcode-implementer runner, WPGB work through the wpgb-specialist, and the preflight discovery evidence through the cpt-codebase-analyst (skippable only against a recorded verified reference baseline) plus the cpt-figma-analyst when a design source exists, per the agent-routing Rule.

skills.name: section-preview-harness
skills.description: Project-local WST Section preview pages: one Section rendered in isolation under /section-preview/<section>/<variant> from Git-tracked JSON fixtures through the real WST render path, with the proven reference implementation. Two jobs kept apart: the one-time bootstrap (harness files, snippet-loader include with confirmed theme-functions.php edit, and the PROJECT-CONTEXT.md key line section-preview-pages: active as a completion gate) and the per-Section sub-workflow 'Configure a further Section' (exporter config entry, backend review hard stop, export over the route, preview URLs into the work record - no bootstrap, main chat only). Three-state detection from key, harness file, or a real exporter config (missing / active / declined) - files without the key mean active, write the key. Adapted to the shell-less workspace: fixtures are exported over a gated REST export route and written into the repository, rewrites are flushed through the status bridge, and preview URLs count only after a bridge-verified deploy.

skills.name: wst-shortcodes
skills.description: Entry point into the bundled Smart Template Gesamthilfe catalog snapshot (SMART-TEMPLATE-HILFE.md, targeted section loads only) and owner of the four-source proof (catalog, installed runtime, project precedent, rendered HTML) that gates every WST shortcode form new to a project - per form and nesting context (flat, loop-1, loop-2+; a flat precedent proves nothing for nested loops) with the result vocabulary proven / proven except runtime (<context>) as a named runtime risk for the deploy hand-over, the least-runtime-dependency form choice when no test render is possible before the deploy, the project-verified 'Known runtime constraints' (wst_string_replace cannot manipulate dynamic content in loop-2+, wst_variable getters return empty in deep-loop shortcode content, loop post IDs are {{post_id/loopname}}), and the documented open catalog discrepancies.

skills.name: frontend-section-qa
skills.description: Frontend CSS/SCSS pass for a WST Section from the Section work record in the project docs layer: Playwright MCP browser QA loop with Capability Probe and Degraded Mode, injection-proofed iteration against the served page as the main mode, tracked CSS writes, the Visual QA Targets writeback, one bundled deploy pass with hard stop, bridge verification of deployed_commit with a bounded retry and abort budget, and the one-time served check that closes the work. Two-stage reaction to an unreconciled project CSS setup: warn once when PROJECT-CONTEXT.md carries css_setup pending, hard stop with a route to project-css-setup when the layout preflight measures an actual container mismatch — never Section-local compensation. Structured as an Execution Gate first (main chat: work record, resolved Preview URLs - unresolved with an active harness is a route-back, spawn exactly one cpt-visual-implementer, stop until return) and a 'Runner execution (cpt-visual-implementer only)' part (preflight with the playwright-browser-claim availability ladder, workflow, injection loop, writeback), followed by the main-chat deploy pass, bridge verification, served check, and commit gate; the non-reasons for skipping the runner are spelled out per the runner-gate Rule.

skills.name: cpt-frontend-qa
skills.description: Frontend CSS/SCSS pass for a WST Custom Post Type from the CPT work record in the project docs layer: per-surface injection-proofed iteration (card, archive/grid, carousel/filter, WPGB output, optional single) as the main mode, the Playwright MCP browser QA loop, one bundled deploy pass with hard stop, bridge verification of deployed_commit with a bounded retry and abort budget, and the one-time served check on the display and single URLs. Generic theme output on a single URL means the Smart Template assignment is pending — an admin step handed to the user, never a CSS debugging round. Structured as an Execution Gate first (main chat: work record, spawn one cpt-visual-implementer per surface, stop until return) and a 'Runner execution (cpt-visual-implementer only)' part (preflight with the playwright-browser-claim availability ladder, per-surface workflow, injection loop, writeback), followed by the main-chat deploy pass, bridge verification, served check, and commit gate; the non-reasons for skipping the runner are spelled out per the runner-gate Rule.

skills.name: wp-media-import

Replaces the legacy WP-CLI media import; there is no server shell in the SmartFlow workspace.

skills.name: content

Successor of the zip /content command; not for new layouts, templates, or CSS.

The docs layer absorbs the legacy handoff files.

Also the post-types worker template inside an auto-docs run.

Core rule: every wst_ shortcode that reads a field from the database needs id='{{post_id}}'; carries the open {{post.id}} vs {{post_id}} catalog validation, the nesting cross-reference, and the wso- markup conventions. Under orchestration, card-template PHP writes route through the wst-shortcode-implementer, WPGB grid/card configuration to the wpgb-specialist, and card CSS stays with cpt-frontend-qa, per the agent-routing Rule.

skills.name: wst-nested-shortcodes
skills.description: Suffix rules for nesting enclosing wst_ shortcodes (wst_if, wst_acf_repeater, wst_is_mobile, ...): same-named nested shortcodes break the WordPress parser silently, so nested levels get unique suffixes _a, _b, _c including else clauses and negated forms; siblings may reuse suffixes, self-closing shortcodes never need one, and the strict named-level chain from the wst-conditional-nesting Rule holds until the suffix-skip question is validated at runtime.

skills.name: smarttags
skills.description: SmartTag {{...}} placeholder syntax of WST: conversion commands with the exactly-one-pipe rule and & chaining, loop context id='{{post_id/<loop-name>}}' and {{row_id/...}}, nested SmartTags, attachment metadata placeholders, SmartTags as variables, and wst_foreach — with the full command list deferred to catalog section 5.24 in the wst-shortcodes snapshot.

skills.name: headline-filling
skills.description: Rules for filling title and subtitle fields in WST Flexible Content blocks: the Format field sets the semantic HTML tag, the Style field sets the wso- look class, heading levels are never skipped, exactly one h1 per page, and design looks that would violate the hierarchy are solved through Style, never by bending the Format.

skills.name: grill-me
skills.description: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design until shared understanding, one question at a time with a recommended answer, exploring project context, docs layer, codebase, and status bridge before asking. Output is a prefilled Section or CPT work-record draft in the project docs layer (or a written decision log for non-WST plans) with explicit unresolved placeholders instead of invented values. Runs in the main chat by design; the workflow preflights of wst-section-workflow and wst-new-post-type stay authoritative. Adapted from the legacy wst-builder grill-me: handoff drafts are replaced by work-record drafts.

skills.name: figma-page-builder
skills.description: Build or remodel a WordPress/WST page from a Figma page frame by reusing the project's existing Flexible Content Sections, WPGB surfaces, media, and global elements: parallel Figma/codebase discovery, a binding ordered page map with surface classification (global, existing-wst, existing-wpgb, content-only, structural-gap), REST content population per the content Skill with backup and fingerprint guard, bridge cache flush, and structural plus visual acceptance. At preflight the anchored Confluence page is re-read fresh for the page-relevant extract (clean skip without anchor, per the confluence-source Rule). Owns page composition, not Section development.

skills.name: jira-ticket-workflow
skills.description: Process a single WESEO Jira ticket (WP-key) end to end in the local SmartFlow workspace: step 0 gate check that routes open mandatory gates to the bundled setup-ticket-ready Skill (the colleague only pastes the ticket link), Atlassian MCP intake with the mandatory screenshot rule (jira_get_issue_images, never blind visual diagnosis) and a fresh run-start read of the ticket-relevant section of the anchored Confluence page (clean skip without anchor, per the confluence-source Rule), triage/routing to the bundled Skills and subagents, diagnosis with mandatory before-measurement of target and reference for comparison tickets and a one-sentence acceptance criterion that verification re-measures (ambiguous intent is asked, never guessed), minimal child-theme fix (project utilities and modifiers before new rules, a user-named fix direction binding), Playwright injection-proof verification with honest proof-mode reporting (marker-verified served check on projects without a bridge or with deployed_commit null), German report with approval gate, then one commit per ticket staging only the ticket's files (never push, foreign working-tree changes reported and left untouched; in the legacy 'master - user commits' state the agent only prepares and the colleague commits), a calm, plainly worded German Jira solution comment with hash and file paths in the work record instead of the ticket, and an optional ticket transition on request (intake question, default no; Done-category transition read from jira_get_transitions after the comment, never guessed). Jira site URL and project key come from PROJECT-CONTEXT.md.

skills.name: jira-batch-workflow
skills.description: Orchestrate a batch of open Jira subtasks (default 10) of one parent task: JQL intake over statusCategory To Do only, screenshot-based triage, untracked statusboard under .cursor/jira-batch/, up to three parallel background jira-ticket-runner leaves with file-disjoint write ownership and chain serialization, feedback relay via resume, serialized per-ticket commits under an explicit batch commit mandate asked at intake (never push, never without the mandate or an individual confirmation), a git status baseline taken at intake with the Working Tree Discipline for unexpected files (checked against the baseline, reported by path, asked from the plausible runner via resume, never git restore), final batch review, Jira solution comments after the user closes the review, and the optional ticket transition on request (intake question next to the mandate, default no, recorded as transition: ja | nein in the board header; Done-category transition read from jira_get_transitions, only for commented tickets). Router and closer only; per-ticket semantics stay in jira-ticket-workflow, while model routing, the fixed return contract, and the handoff schema come from the agent-routing Rule.

Anchors the page as part of the run when setup never recorded one; secrets become placeholders plus pointer; runs in the main chat by design.

agents.name: cpt-codebase-analyst

Supplies the wst-new-post-type preflight evidence on every foundation or remodel start, including the reference CPT's content model (Flexible Content clone, single partial, Smart Template include) and the existing FC layouts, and reports a dropped FC clone or a typed-only CPT facing page Sections as an OPEN DECISION; skippable only against a recorded verified reference baseline and Project Layout Profile.

agents.name: cpt-figma-analyst

agents.name: wst-shortcode-implementer

Chooses the least-runtime-dependent WST form when source 4 of the four-source proof cannot be reached before the deploy and reports the gate as four-source: proven except runtime (<context>); stops with OPEN DECISION: foundation not confirmed when a remodel assignment lacks the user's foundation confirmation.

agents.name: cpt-visual-implementer

Accepts three inputs: a fresh start, 'Resume with current file state' (a half-finished CSS file from the main chat is verified and continued, never restarted or discarded), and an agent-routing handoff file.
